narrative_before: This is a documented CTID emulation of FIN7, modelling the group's real 2017-2018 spearphishing campaigns against hospitality, restaurant and gaming targets (based on MITRE ATT&CK Evaluations, Round 2). The lab is a four-host domain: domain controller 'hoteldc', hotel manager workstation 'hotelmanager', IT admin workstation 'itadmin', and accounting workstation 'accounting'. A spearphishing attachment compromises hotelmanager; FIN7 delays malware execution, assesses the target, stages an interactive toolkit, and escalates privileges with a modified Mimikatz (samcat). The actor expands access using paexec/process-hollowing to move to the itadmin workstation, then RDPs from itadmin to the accounting workstation, establishes shim persistence, and uses BOOSTWRITE DLL-hijacking for user monitoring before stealing payment data from a fake payment application (AccountingIQ.exe).
